method: Independent re-implementation (scratchpad/lens2/multi_tf/verify/v_outcomes.py: own Wilder ATR14, own isolated-margin liquidation/sizing math, own 15m bar-loop exit engine; v_sim.py: own one-position account simulator) on 8 strategies (core N01_ST_EMA, N02_ST_KST, DOGE, S2_ST_ROC, N20_EMA9_CHOP, OBV_S; DeepSeek F5_BOX, F11_RAID) x 6 coins x 15m/30m/1h/4h, 2023-10-01..2026-09-29 (3 years, 262,780 distinct signal outcomes). Per-signal parity with the study's outc cache: 262,780/262,780 matched, 0 with |dR|>1e-3, leverage agrees 99.997% (v_parity.py). Account parity (v_cmp.py, 2023-11..2026-08 to skip warm-up): trade counts and mean R identical for A|FC, ALL|SWH, HI|FC, ALL|SW, ALL|LTF in all 8 strategies. Mechanics therefore reproduce exactly; disagreements below are about metrics and interpretation. Look-ahead: none found (entry = first 15m open after the signal bar closes, exact timestamp alignment enforced; ATR of the closed signal bar; sizing uses only signal-time data; trader freed only for entries after the exit bar). Bars/brackets/fee model are the study's inputs (not re-derived). Large intermediates (outc.csv, v_trades.csv.gz, v_blocked.csv.gz) deleted; rerun v_outcomes.py then v_sim.py (~1.5 min) to regenerate.

verdicts.recomputed: 3y subset, own sim, pooled per setup (core6 / ds2): net R/trade A|FC -0.147 / -0.173, ALL|FC -0.135 / -0.164, ALL|SWH -0.122 / -0.138, HI|FC -0.081 / -0.114; gross R +0.000..+0.010 (core), -0.011..-0.025 (ds); cost 0.154/0.123/0.089 (core A/C/HI). Every strategy x setup negative (0 of 175 cells positive, v_sim_rows.csv).
verdicts.note: Gross ~0 and net ~ -cost reproduce. The two DeepSeek definitions in the sample have slightly negative gross (-0.01..-0.025), so for them the hurdle is a bit above cost.

verdicts.recomputed: Paired vs A|FC (week-cluster bootstrap, 3y): core ALL|SWH +0.024 [+0.016,+0.033] (6/6), ALL|FC +0.012 [+0.006,+0.018] (6/6), HI|FC +0.066 [+0.050,+0.085] (6/6); ds ALL|SWH +0.034 [+0.019,+0.048], HI +0.059 [+0.032,+0.085]. Decomposition core ALL|SWH-A: dgross -0.007, dcost -0.031 (pure cost). Last 91 days (core6): cost A 0.194, ALL|SWH 0.148, HI 0.107 (study 0.197/0.152/0.107).
verdicts.note: Per-trade hurdle numbers reproduce. Caveat (see MT6/MT10): the per-trade metric is not the account result. Per day, the C-proxy pays about the same total cost as B (core6 0.683 vs 0.664 R/day with the same tie rule).

verdicts.recomputed: core6 3y: A|FC 5.31 trades/day from 29.5 signals/day, ALL|SWH 5.56 from 33.9, HI 1.53 from 4.45 (these 6 are busier than the 35 average). 60-day MDE i.i.d. A 0.133R, C 0.104R, HI 0.197R; week-cluster design effect 1.05 / 1.02 / 0.95, so clustered MDE 0.136 / 0.105 / 0.193.
verdicts.note: Counts and MDE arithmetic reproduce. Inside one trader, time clustering barely inflates the MDE because only one position is open at a time, so the study's warning that real MDEs are larger is small for one trader. It matters for pooling traders on overlapping strategies. An AI-vs-shadow comparison with two independent arms needs about x1.4 the MDE.

verdicts.recomputed: Blocked (non-tie) share core6: A|FC 74% (+8% ties), ALL|SWH 74% (+10%), HI 54% (+12%); ds2 69% / 69% / 48%. Blocked alone-R vs taken: core A -0.168 vs -0.147; ds -0.188 vs -0.173. Within the same tf it still holds: core A 15m blocked -0.184 vs taken -0.159, 30m -0.133 vs -0.115.
verdicts.note: Reproduces. Blocked signals are slightly WORSE than taken ones even within a timeframe, so under rules one-position blocking is mildly helpful. This is about rule signals and says nothing about AI ranking skill.

verdicts.recomputed: ALL|FC core6: 25.9% of blocked 15m/30m signals were blocked by a 1h/4h position (ds2 24.1%; study 23%). 15m signals blocked during a 4h hold -0.273R (n 4,866) vs -0.177R when blocked by a 15m position (n 50,486); ds -0.254 vs -0.212.

Switch-to-any is worst: core ALL|SW - ALL|FC -0.030 [-0.040,-0.020] (0/6), A|SW - A|FC -0.026 (0/6); per day -3.12 vs -0.69 R/day. Switched-out trades: R at switch -0.152 vs held-alone -0.152, so the early close itself costs ~0 and the extra round trip is the loss (study's costing reproduces: exit taker+slip at the next 15m open, new entry with its own cost). BUT 'switch only to higher tf is best' holds only per trade and is confounded: sim.py runs SWH with longer-tf-first tie order and FC with coin/shorter-tf-first order. With the tie rule held fixed, core ALL|SWH - ALL|LTF = +0.005 [-0.002,+0.012] (4/6) on my subset (study's own 5y res: +0.007/trade, 29/35). Per day (fixed risk per trade = account P&L), switching up LOSES MORE: study's own 5y res files, core ALL|SWH vs ALL|LTF -0.019 R/day (SWH better in only 10/35; ds 10/44); A|SWH vs A|FC -0.037 R/day (better in 4/35). Own subset: ALL|SWH -0.681 vs ALL|LTF -0.629 R/day; A|SWH -0.830 vs A|FC -0.779.
verdicts.note: SWH adds round trips (about 1.1-1.5 switches/day). Its lower cost per trade comes from moving into 1h/4h holds, but the account pays more total cost per day. It is the better rule only if the AI's per-trade edge is above the hurdle. At zero edge, no-switch with longer-tf-first ties (B/LTF) is the cheaper account. The +0.015R 'SWH vs FC' figure is about one-third tie-rule effect (LTF vs FC +0.005).

verdicts.recomputed: Own sizing math (v_feas.py) reproduces the bar shares exactly: 4h 20x 19.2% (5y) / 25.6% (last 30d), 30x 0.9% / 0%; 1h 20x 77.6% / 89.8%, 30x 25.9% / 32.6%; 4h 20x by coin 5y/30d BTC 56/100, ETH 25/53, SOL 4/0, DOGE 7/0, LTC 14/0.5, BCH 9/0. 15m house 50x 7.0% (5y), 40x 34%, 30x 80%; 30m 40x 13%, 50x 2%. 4h signals in the 3y subset: 24.3% sizable at 30x/20x; forced 20x without the buffer gate: liquidation price inside the stop for 38.8%, and 4.4% exit at the initial stop, i.e. would be liquidated first (3y, quieter; verify_costs 8.1% on 5y). 1h: 16.7% of signals not sizable at 20x/30x.
verdicts.note: The numbers are right, but the headline '20-50x is executable on 15m (and mostly 30m)' is wrong by the study's own feas.csv. Under house rules, 50x sizes on only 7% of 15m bars (11% last 30d) and 40x on 34%. On 30m, 40x sizes on 13% and 50x on 2%. Only 20-30x is broadly executable on 15m/30m. This agrees with verify_costs: both show 4h at 20x needs the per-signal gate (stop + 1 ATR inside liquidation). The study's 19% sizable share is the gated version of verify_costs' 8.1% liquidate-first figure, and the two do not conflict.

verdicts.recomputed: Demeaned R, 91-day windows, 1% risk (own code): core6 A|FC median DD 20.3%, >25% in 25.6% of windows; ALL|SWH 16.7% / 12.0%; HI 7.5% / 0%; ds2 A 18.9% / 26.9%, ALL|SWH 13.1% / 7.7%, HI 6.7% / 0%. With the actual drift at 1% risk: >25% DD in 92% of A windows, 95% of ALL|SWH windows, 4% of HI windows.
verdicts.note: Reproduces (my A numbers are a little higher because the sample strategies trade more). Only about 12 windows per strategy in 3 years, so the window shares are coarse. The zero-net-edge assumption is generous: a rule-level trader (gross 0, cost paid) breaches 25% in about 9 of 10 quarters at 1% risk on A/C.

verdicts.recomputed: Arithmetic from pooled.csv reproduces: A|FC core 4.24 entries + 4.24 x 2.58 h x 2 = 21.9 hold checks = 26/day; all-signal 24.9 + 21.9 = 47; 30 traders x 26..47 x 30 x $0.03 = $714..$1,279/month. Design doc v2 sec. 14-1 gives $0.03 per Sonnet call, or about $0.015 with good caching.
verdicts.note: With caching at $0.015, the range halves to about $357..$640 for 30 A traders. The lower bound assumes the AI takes every signal it sees while flat; a skip-heavy AI makes more entry calls. The design doc's locked cost rules (one call per bar close per trader, hold wake-ups only on an opposite signal, small model for routine hold checks) are not modelled and would cut hold calls a lot.

verdicts.recomputed: Per trade: C (ALL|SWH) > B > A reproduces (core6 -0.122 / -0.135 / -0.147). Per day (account P&L at fixed risk), study's own 5y res: core mean R/day A|FC -0.622, A|SWH -0.660, ALL|FC -0.556, ALL|SWH -0.540, ALL|LTF -0.521, HI -0.100; ds A -0.744, ALL|SWH -0.618, ALL|LTF -0.600, HI -0.143. ALL|LTF beats ALL|SWH per day in 25/35 core and 34/44 ds strategies.
verdicts.note: 'C best' holds only for the per-trade hurdle. For the account at zero or sub-hurdle edge, B with longer-tf-first ties (no switching) loses less per day than C. A tie rule that takes the widest stop first adds a further +0.014R/trade (core) and +0.019R (ds) on my subset, a free code-level gain. The robust ranking is {B-LTF ~ C} > A, with HI far lowest per day. That HI is lowest is a frequency effect (1.1-1.5 trades/day), not evidence of edge.

strategy_note_problems: 'Lowest-hurdle setup with >= 1 trade/day' (build_json.py line ~195) only compares A|FC, ALL|FC and ALL|SWH, never HI|FC. In 16 of the 35 core notes HI|FC has >= 1 trade/day and a less negative net R than the named setup, yet the note names ALL|SWH or ALL|FC. Examples: DOGE HI 1.21/day -0.061 vs ALL|SWH -0.110; N01_ST_EMA 1.50/day -0.092 vs -0.121; N04_ST_KLINGER 2.85/day -0.070 vs -0.102; N20_EMA9_CHOP 1.43/day -0.084 vs -0.122.

Grades A/B/C (sign of gross R in each half) are at noise level. Example: DOGE gross IS +0.003 / CF +0.016 with SE about 0.014 per half (about 3,750 trades, sd 0.85), t about 0.2 and 1.1. The graded distribution (A 15, B 16, C 15) is close to the 25/50/25 expected if every gross were exactly 0, so the grade should not be read as quality.
Sampled numbers (DOGE, N01_ST_EMA, N02_ST_KST, N20_EMA9_CHOP, OBV_S, S2_ST_ROC, F5_BOX, F11_RAID) reproduce exactly on the overlapping window (v_cmp.py), so no numeric errors were found in the notes.
DeepSeek family notes average 'per def' over definitions that are duplicates (F11_RAID = F11_TSOUP = F13_RAID_PD at 15m, F5_BOX = F5_BOX_HTF, etc.), which double-weights some signal streams.
missed: Per-trade vs per-day metric: every setup ranking uses mean R per trade. At fixed risk per trade the account result is R per day, and by that measure switching (SWH) is worse than not switching (study's own res: ALL|LTF beats ALL|SWH per day in 25/35 core, 34/44 ds). Hurdle per trade and loss per day should both be reported.
Tie-rule confound: SWH and LTF are run with longer-tf-first ties, FC with BTC-first/shorter-tf-first ties, so 'SWH vs FC' mixes the switch effect with the tie effect.

Coin priority on ties (BTC, ETH, SOL, ...) is not neutral. BTC/ETH have the narrowest stops, so they have the highest cost in R. Random ties improve core A|FC by +0.007 [+0.003,+0.012], ALL|FC by +0.010. A widest-stop-first (lowest cost-in-R) tie rule improves A|FC by +0.014 [+0.009,+0.020] core and +0.019 [+0.010,+0.029] ds, and ALL|SWH by +0.007. This is a free code-level rule for any one-position trader, about half the A-to-C gain.

Feasibility filter changes the trade mix: the ALL/A scopes silently drop the 17% of 1h, 5% of 30m and 76% of 4h signals that 30x/20x cannot size. Those dropped signals are the wide-stop, low-cost-in-R ones (ALLINF|FC -0.127 vs ALL|FC -0.136 per trade). Trading them at lower leverage (e.g. 10x) instead of rejecting them is an untested option that lowers the hurdle.

Leverage headline: 40-50x is not broadly executable on 15m/30m under house rules (15m 50x 7%, 40x 34%; 30m 40x 13%). The owners' '20-50x by AI confidence' would mostly fall back to 20-30x unless sizing changes to risk-per-stop.

Hold-call cost: the design doc's own locked call-reduction rules (one call per bar close, hold wake-ups only on opposite signals, small model for routine checks, $0.015 with caching) are not modelled, so the $/month estimates are an upper-middle range, not a floor.

Overlapping strategies: AI traders on duplicate or near-duplicate definitions would hold the same positions (verify_costs), so pooled CIs across strategies are too narrow and 30 seats are fewer independent experiments than they look.
